macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street futures rebound as AI stocks recover
items.summary: U.S. equity futures rose sharply Monday after last week’s selloff: Dow futures gained about 1.8%, S&P 500 futures 2.5%, and Nasdaq futures 3.3%. Nvidia climbed roughly 8.7% as investors returned to beaten-down technology shares.[1][3]

items.title: Markets focus on upcoming PCE inflation report and December Fed decision
items.summary: Investors are awaiting Wednesday’s personal-consumption-expenditures inflation report for clues about monetary policy. Markets were pricing roughly a 95% probability of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December, though that expectation weakened after the recent selloff.[2][3]

items.title: Chicago Fed activity index weakens
items.summary: The Chicago Fed National Activity Index fell to -0.06 in October from 0.05 previously, below the 0.20 consensus forecast, indicating softer U.S. economic activity.[1]

items.title: CrowdStrike agrees to acquire Zscaler
items.summary: CrowdStrike announced an all-stock acquisition of Zscaler valued at approximately $43.9 billion. Zscaler shares rose more than 19% in premarket trading, while the deal reshaped the cybersecurity sector.[1][3]
items.source: MT Newswires and Reuters via Fidelity

items.title: Amazon reportedly nears $7.5 billion Decart acquisition
items.summary: Amazon shares gained about 3.3% after a report that the company is nearing a $7.5 billion deal to acquire AI startup Decart, highlighting continued large-scale investment in artificial intelligence.[1]

items.title: Tesla rises on Full Self-Driving rollout plans
items.summary: Tesla shares gained roughly 4.9% after Elon Musk said the company is preparing a broad release of Full Self-Driving version 15 in December.[1]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $61,000 after sharp sell-off
items.summary: Bitcoin recovered above $61,000 after falling near $55,000 in a weekend sell-off that triggered roughly $1.8 billion in forced liquidations. Ethereum also rose about 2% to above $1,715, while Bitcoin remained down more than 20% for the month.[1]

items.title: SEC sues eight entities over alleged $37 million crypto fraud
items.summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission charged eight Colorado-based entities, alleging they defrauded more than 1,500 investors of approximately $37.45 million through fake investment advisers and cryptocurrency trading platforms.[3][4]

items.title: Chainflip freezes withdrawals after suspected $4.86 million vault loss
items.summary: Cross-chain liquidity protocol Chainflip placed its network in Safe Mode and froze withdrawals after approximately $4.86 million disappeared from an Ethereum vault. South Korean exchanges Upbit and Bithumb also suspended CYBER token transfers amid a suspected bridge exploit.[1]

items.title: UK brings qualifying stablecoin issuance under regulated framework
items.summary: The United Kingdom enacted amendments to its cryptoasset regime that classify qualifying stablecoin issuance as a regulated activity and require issuers to maintain a UK establishment.[1][6]

items.title: South Korea prepares comprehensive cryptocurrency legislation
items.summary: South Korea is expected to publish a draft of comprehensive cryptocurrency legislation this week, potentially affecting market structure and the regulatory outlook for crypto platforms operating in the country.[10]

items.title: JPMorgan and DBS expand tokenized-dollar payments
items.summary: JPMorgan and DBS reportedly introduced round-the-clock tokenized-dollar payment capabilities for the U.S.–Singapore corridor, highlighting continued institutional development of blockchain-based settlement infrastructure.[4]

items.title: Hyperliquid weekly revenue exceeds $21 million
items.summary: Hyperliquid generated approximately $21.22 million in revenue over the past week, with about $3.22 million recorded in the latest 24-hour period, according to DeFiLlama data cited in the report.[3]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Sarvam releases Sarvam-105B-1711 open-weight model
items.summary: Sarvam released a 105-billion-parameter open-weight model focused on agentic tasks, instruction following, tool use, and Indian languages. A daily AI roundup reports an average score of 73.9 across eight agent benchmarks at an estimated cost of about $0.15 per million tokens.

items.title: DiffuSpace releases Clover-35B diffusion language model
items.summary: DiffuSpace released Clover-35B-A3B-Preview, a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model, along with its weights and code. The project reports a 73.6 score on SWE-bench Verified, highlighting continued experimentation with alternatives to autoregressive language models.

items.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini
items.summary: Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weight 26.4-billion-parameter model designed to perform additional internal computation before answering. The model has about 3.4 billion active parameters per token and is positioned for local, agentic use.

items.title: Tencent releases Hy4 multimodal model
items.summary: Tencent released Hy4, an open-weight model supporting text, image, and video inputs with a reported million-token context window. Its architecture reportedly contains 770 billion parameters, with 49 billion activated per token.

items.title: Z.ai launches GLM-5.4 coding and vision model
items.summary: Z.ai launched GLM-5.4, described as a 750-billion-parameter model using a Loop Transformer architecture, with vision and coding improvements. Access was reportedly opened to GLM Coding Plan subscribers.

items.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron-Labs-Sigma diffusion models
items.summary: NVIDIA released the Nemotron-Labs-Sigma family of continuous diffusion language models, adding to the industry’s growing exploration of diffusion-based approaches for language generation.

items.title: Microsoft launches licensed weights for custom AI models
items.summary: Microsoft announced MAI Licensed Weights, a program intended to make selected model weights available for organizations building customized AI systems. The announcement reflects growing demand for models that can be adapted and deployed under enterprise-specific requirements.

items.title: OpenAI reports progress on mathematical theorem proving
items.summary: OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra was reported to have produced a Lean proof of Smoktunowicz’s gap theorem, marking a notable development in machine-assisted formal mathematics. The result remains a reported research milestone rather than evidence that broader mathematical claims have been independently validated.

items.title: Argonne adds Tara and Minerva supercomputers to inference service
items.summary: Argonne National Laboratory added the Tara and Minerva supercomputers to its inference service, expanding access to high-performance computing resources for AI model inference and research.

items.title: Walmart enables Meta AI agent shopping
items.summary: Walmart reportedly enabled Meta’s Muse AI agent to shop and complete purchases on Walmart.com for users. The move highlights the continuing shift from conversational assistants toward agents capable of executing transactions.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: GTA VI reportedly breaks entertainment launch records
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI reportedly generated billions of dollars in its opening period and sold tens of millions of copies, making it the dominant gaming-industry story of the past day.

items.title: GTA VI receives first patch on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S
items.summary: Rockstar released an initial post-launch update for Grand Theft Auto VI on current-generation consoles.

items.title: Microsoft announces 20 Xbox releases for the week
items.summary: Microsoft revealed a slate of 20 games scheduled to launch on Xbox platforms during the week of November 23.

items.title: Ubisoft establishes AI-focused subsidiary
items.summary: The team behind Ubisoft’s first playable AI-based research-and-development project has reportedly been organized as a separate subsidiary called Motherbrain.

items.title: Supercell targets creator of AI cheat for Clash Royale
items.summary: Supercell reportedly took action against a creator of an AI-powered Clash Royale cheat as part of efforts to identify and combat cheating.

items.title: Hellraiser: Revival wins Horror Game Awards top prize
items.summary: Hellraiser: Revival reportedly won Game of the Year at the Horror Game Awards, while Resident Evil Requiem collected four awards.

items.title: QoR advances in VCT Americas competition
items.summary: QoR advanced to the VCT Americas Kickoff North American playoffs after sweeping Maryville in its matchup.
